name: Kedarnath Temple
description: One of the twelve Jyotirlingas, dedicated to Lord Shiva. Situated at 3,583 meters in the Rudraprayag district of Uttarakhand, it is the highest among the 12 Jyotirlingas.
historicalSignificance: Built by the Pandavas around 8,000 years ago according to legend. The current structure dates to the 8th century when Adi Shankaracharya revived it.

name: Badrinath Temple
description: The most sacred pilgrimage site for Hindus, dedicated to Lord Vishnu. Located at 3,133 meters in the Chamoli district along the Alaknanda River.
historicalSignificance: Established by Adi Shankaracharya in the 8th century. One of the four Char Dhams of Hindu pilgrimage. The temple is closed for six months due to extreme winter.

name: Somnath Temple
description: The first of the twelve Jyotirlingas, located on the western coast of Gujarat. Rebuilt multiple times, the current temple was completed in 1951.
historicalSignificance: Destroyed and rebuilt several times by Mahmud of Ghazni, Allauddin Khalji, and Aurangzeb. Each destruction and rebuilding symbolizes the resilience of dharma.

name: Konark Sun Temple
description: A 13th-century temple dedicated to the Sun God, built by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga Dynasty. Shaped as a colossal chariot with elaborately carved stone wheels.
historicalSignificance: A masterpiece of Odishan architecture and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The temple's alignment precisely tracks the sun's path.

name: Kailash Temple
description: A monumental rock-cut temple at Ellora, carved from a single basalt cliff. Dedicated to Shiva, it represents Mount Kailash, the abode of Lord Shiva.
historicalSignificance: Carved between 757-783 CE under the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I. Considered one of the most remarkable cave temples in the world.

name: Ramanathaswamy Temple
description: A Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, located on Rameshwaram Island in Tamil Nadu. Part of the Char Dham pilgrimage and one of the twelve Jyotirlingas.
historicalSignificance: According to the Ramayana, Rama worshipped Shiva here after returning from Lanka. Built by the Pandavas and later expanded by the Chola kings.
